standard_prerequisites.name: Universal function and s-m-n theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: Un(f(x),y) = phi_{f(x)}(y), and s-m-n gives f with phi_{f(x)}(y) = g(x,y) for any partial computable g.
standard_prerequisites.use: Direction (1)=>(2) unpacks via Un; direction (2)=>(1) manufactures f from g by s-m-n.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1165-1180): (1) every partial computable g(x,y) has an index e with phi_e(y) = g(e,y) iff (2) every computable f(x) has an index e with phi_e(y) = phi_{f(e)}(y).
(1) => (2) (proof lines 1182-1190): given f set g(x,y) = Un(f(x),y); an index e for g gives phi_e(y) = Un(f(e),y) = phi_{f(e)}(y).
(2) => (1) (lines 1191-1198): given g, s-m-n yields f with phi_{f(x)}(y) = g(x,y); an index e for f gives phi_e(y) = phi_{f(e)}(y) = g(e,y).
proof_roadmap: Prove (1)=>(2) by instantiating (1) with Un composed with f.
Prove (2)=>(1) by producing f from g via s-m-n and instantiating (2).
Both chains are two displayed equalities each.
difficulty_reason: Equivalence of two fixed-point formulations (statement 1165-1180, proof 1182-1198): both directions fully carried with displayed equality chains. H2.
